questions.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(6,-1),(-4,1),(3,5).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(-6,-1)$
- $(4,-1)$
- $(3,-5)$
questions.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${180}^{∘}$ is given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{{180}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{{180}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-6,1),(4,-1),(-3,-5).$ 

So, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem:

- $(-4,3)$
- $(-2,2)$
- $(-1,-3)$

The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-\pi }$ by an angle of $\pi $ radians is the same as counterclockwise rotation by the same angle. It's given by the matrix

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-\pi },$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-\pi }$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-4,3),(-2,2),(-1,-3).$

So, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

questions.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(-2,-1),(1,3),(2,-3).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${270}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(-3,1)$
- $(-3,2)$
- $(1,-2)$
questions.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by an angle of ${270}^{∘}$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of ${90}^{∘}.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
R[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under ${R}_{-{270}^{∘}}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(1,-2),(-3,1),(3,2).$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."

- $(-2,1)$

- $(-4,3)$

- $(-5,3)$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The counterclockwise rotation $\mathbf{R}_{\pi}$ by an angle of $\pi$ radians is given by the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of $\mathbf{R}_{\pi},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S$ as columns:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -1 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $\mathbf{R}_{\pi}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4 \\ -1 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -5 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $S'$ are $(-2,1), (3,-5), (-4,3).$

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."

\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =Ai=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j \\ {j}^{′} & =Aj=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039248/assets/414cb72ff004fe4c5898a0e2c7b60b4b3651473e776388fad21efd8fc9ae6165.png)

So, the matrix represents a rotation of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.

Therefore, in order to find $A\mathbf{v},$ we need to rotate $\mathbf{v}$ counterclockwise by an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ radians, as shown below.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Using a Matrix That Represents a Rotation of 90 Degrees
canonical_examples.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at  $(-5,-1), (1,4), (3,-5).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of $S',$ the image of $S$ under the **clockwise** rotation $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ}$ by an angle of $90^\circ$ about the origin?

- $(1,-5)$

- $(4,-1)$

- $(-5,-3)$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The clockwise rotation $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ}$ by an angle of $90^\circ$ is the same as counterclockwise rotation by an angle of $270^\circ.$ It's given by the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the action of $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ},$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S$ as columns:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $\mathbf{R}_{-90^\circ}$ by calculating the matrix product $RX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & -5 \\ 5 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $S'$ are $(-1,5), (4,-1), (-5,-3).$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."
